baseline.libgphoto2_ref: main of ian-morgan99/libgphoto2; v106's pin. It is an ancestor of the 9ec24138d used here, so every driver change since v106 is included rather than replaced.
baseline.patcher_ref: main of ian-morgan99/benro-polaris-firmware-patcher; v106's pin. 20 commits behind the edc5f4d used here.

purpose: Ship the plate-solve diagnostics and timeout classification from issue #321, which v106 does not contain, together with three corrections to the release process itself. v106 was built from a patcher commit that is merged to main but 20 commits behind it, so its copy of polaris-autosolve.sh and polaris-align.sh predates #321 entirely. Every gate read green because R3 only proves ancestry, never currency. This candidate is built from the current tips of both repos and is the first release checked by a gate that compares the shipped on-disk scripts against the commit the build claims.

changes.summary: polaris-autosolve.sh now logs plate-solve duration alongside frame dimensions and downsample factor. A solve that timed out previously left no record of how long it ran, so 'slow but eventually fine', 'burned the whole cpulimit' and 'failed in milliseconds' were indistinguishable in the log. Dimensions are captured during the polaris-extract pass that already runs, rather than paying for a second pass on this CPU, and handed across the subshell boundary via /tmp/polaris-frame-dims because solve_frame calls pick_downsample as $(...) where an assigned variable would be invisible to the caller.

polaris-align.sh classifies independent-search timeouts as TIMEOUT instead of reporting 'no match'. search_exhausted remains a distinct non-match so the two stay distinguishable in both directions. Found on hardware, not in source: a real run printed 'failure_reason:no match ... 50.37s rc=7' beside a solver line saying failure_reason:timeout.

polaris-autosolve.sh and polaris-align.sh in this packet differ from v106's by digest. Verified directly against the built v106 artifact: its polaris-autosolve.sh is 5b1a551e... with zero occurrences of FRAME_DIMS_FILE, where main has 6d59045e... with three.

check-release-gates.py gained R5, which compares every file in container/astro/ondisk/ against the copy inside the built bundle and against origin/main restricted to shipped paths. It fails closed when it cannot locate the shipped scripts or compares zero files. Without it a build can be merged and still ship payload 20 commits behind main while every gate reports green.

build-doctor.sh section 3 is titled 'at a reachable pin' and RELEASE-ENTRYPOINTS.md advertises that it checks the pin is reachable from origin, but the script never contacted origin. It read refs/remotes/origin/main off disk and tested ancestry against that, so a months-old ref printed OK having judged nothing, and a good pin could be reported orphaned against a stale tip. It now queries origin, refreshes when behind, judges against the live tip, and reports SKIP rather than OK when origin is unreachable.

The bundle README.txt generated by build-astro.sh told users to run 'scp -r COPY-TO-SD-CARD-ROOT/. root@<polaris ip>:/app/sd/' under the heading 'the same layout works'. This device's sshd has no sftp-server subsystem: scp dies with 'Connection closed' and legacy scp -O hangs. It shipped in every bundle including v106. Replaced with scripts/release/install-astro-kit.sh, and the command is deliberately not printed because it looks runnable and users copy it.

Driver moves from 530c879fe to 9ec24138d. The only non-docs change in that range is examples/pentax-persistent-config-benchmark.c, where a failed restore readback no longer exits 0. camlibs/ptp2/ is byte-identical between the two, so ptp2.so is unchanged from v106 and no protocol behaviour differs.
Twelve new tests, each verified to fail against the pre-fix version of the file it covers. Registered in PY_TESTS so the gate's test-list drift guard runs them.

known_limits: NOT INSTALLED AND NOT DEPLOYABLE YET. The device has been unreachable since the 2026-11-12 host-to-device WiFi fault: 64 KB over ssh stalls and a raw nc upload received 41,992 of 256 KB, while a 2 MB download in the other direction completed in 13.5 s. wlan0 showed rxerr=27775 txerr=0. The SD card is not at fault; dd of 40 MB and then 86 MB to /app/sd both completed at 2.1-2.4 MB/s with zero mmc drop events. A reboot did not clear it.

The mandatory device gates have NOT run: the install hash checks against the immutable install-manifest.json, and the physical Benro Connect / Manual / Bulb regression. Offline gate green means OFFLINE-QUALIFIED only.

R5 covers container/astro/ondisk/, which is what ships verbatim as shell payload. It does not cover the C sources compiled inside the container (polaris-httpd.c, polaris-solve.c and friends); those are rebuilt from the tree every time so they cannot be stale in the same way, but a bug introduced in them would not be caught by R5.
R5 compares against origin/main at the moment the gate runs. It proves the packet matches main then; it does not prove main itself is correct.

The driver pin 9ec24138d carries no ptp2 behaviour change over v106, so this candidate is not a camera-behaviour release. The Pentax K-1 II rig remains wedged since 2026-11-09 and no hardware confirmation of anything in the ColorTemp 0xd018 domain has been obtained.

Issue #164 remains open. Slider bounds 2500-10000 step 10 are now confirmed in IT2 2.6.2.5 via BAML, but those are a UI constraint, not device evidence, so the allowlist still needs a direct-host session before it can be called a proven domain.
validation_focus: Confirm installed build_id and both source commits with scripts/verify-installed-build.sh once the device is reachable.
Confirm polaris-autosolve.sh on the device matches this build's copy byte-for-byte, and that a solve line now carries duration and frame dimensions.
Force an independent-search timeout and confirm the log says TIMEOUT rather than 'no match', with search_exhausted still distinguishable.
Run check-release-gates.py against this packet and confirm R5 reports OK, not just that it did not error.
Physical Benro Connect / Manual / Bulb regression, which no offline check substitutes for.
Re-run the astro kit install after any flash, since flashing replaces appfs and removes both the plate solver and its boot hook.
